sets.name: 1 Paper body
sets.title: A record against the body of its paper
sets.context: Our records are read from abstracts. For papers with a free full text, a second program compared each record with the body of the paper. The records here passed our other checks, and that program said the body contradicts them.
sets.question: Our record passes our checks, and a check against the full text says the body of the paper contradicts it. What happened?

answers.label: abstract says more than the body shows
answers.meaning: The record reads the abstract correctly. The body's own test or text does not show the result, or shows less.

answers.label: record misreads the abstract
answers.meaning: The abstract does not say what the record says.

answers.label: no real contradiction
answers.meaning: The record and the body agree in substance: for example the outcome is a group of measures, or one number differs while the direction agrees.

answers.label: cannot tell
answers.meaning: The texts shown, and the paper behind the link, do not settle it.

exercise  vs  nutrition
Outcome: irisin
Direction (first against second): higher

It was determined that the body composition components, lipid profile indicators, insulin, glucose, insulin resistance, leptin, ghrelin, irisin, and MDA parameters examined in this study showed positive changes in the intervention groups. Group E had a greater effect on body muscle percentage, MDA, and irisin levels, while group N had a greater effect on blood lipids and ghrelin levels.
items.extra: What the full-text check said: E and N have the same significance letter for irisin change, so their reported comparison is not significant.

75%CAPS  vs  75%Control
Outcome: respiratory quotient (RQ)
Direction (first against second): lower
Respiratory quotient (RQ) was more decreased at 75%CAPS (p = 0.04) than at 75%Control (p = 0.05) when compared with 100%Control.

No significant differences in RQ were seen between the two conditions in energy balance (100%CAPS 0.92±0.02 and 100%Control 0.92±0.02) nor between the two conditions in negative energy balance (75%CAPS 0.89±0.02 and 75%Control 0.90±0.01).
items.extra: What the full-text check said: The body reports no significant RQ difference between the two 75% conditions.

Outcome: fruits
In: males
Direction (first against second): lower
However, we found that males in the restricted sleep condition ate more added sugar, more carbohydrates, and fewer fruits than when in healthy sleep.
In addition, we observed a medium-sized interaction trending toward significance between sex and sleep condition on fruit consumption (p =.086; ηp2 = .052).
items.extra: What the full-text check said: The body identifies the fruit finding as a nonsignificant trend.

tomato diet  vs  control diet
Outcome: serum total cholesterol at 8 weeks
Direction (first against second): lower

The tomato diet group had significantly lower serum total cholesterol, triglyceride, systolic blood pressure and blood sugar, and higher high-density lipoprotein cholesterol than the control diet group.
items.extra: What the full-text check said: At week 8, total cholesterol was numerically higher in the tomato group and the between-group difference was not significant.

Outcome: fatigue symptoms at 8 weeks
Direction (first against second): no difference
For health-related quality of life (HRQoL) indices, emotional functioning and fatigue symptoms were improved after 4 weeks only in the intervention group although no difference was found at week 8.
items.extra: What the full-text check said: Table 5 marks the week-8 between-group difference as significant; the fatigue score was lower with intervention.

KD + exercise  vs  KD only
Outcome: HDL-C at 2 months
Direction (first against second): higher

At 2 months, the observation group demonstrated substantially greater improvements in WSS (1.534 dynes/cm²), NO (4.916 µmol/L) and HDL-C (8.4%), along with reductions in ET-1 (- 3.327 ng/L) and LDL-C (- 12.3%) than the control group (all p < 0.05).
items.extra: What the full-text check said: The table reports no significant between-group difference in HDL-C at 2 months.

water with 250 mg sucralose  vs  water
Outcome: insulin concentrations
Direction (first against second): higher
Insulin concentrations were nominally higher following all NNS conditions without altering glycemia.

No statistically significant differences in active GLP-1, GIP, glucose, insulin, or C-peptide were observed when sucralose (at varying doses mixed in water) was administered before the OGTTs in study arm 1 (Table 2).
items.extra: What the full-text check said: The body reports no significant insulin difference, not higher insulin.

cells:
M. oleifera leaf extract group  vs  placebo group
Outcome: basal metabolic rate
Direction (first against second): higher
Compared with the Con group, the Med group showed a more pronounced decrease in BMI, yet better preserved its basal metabolic rate, muscle mass, and fat-free mass.

After 1 month, compared with those at baseline, fat‐free body weight, muscle mass, and basal metabolic rate decreased by 0.65 kg, 0.6 kg and 49.1 kcal, respectively, in the Con group and by 0.06 kg, 0.06 kg, and 13.12 kcal, respectively, in the Med group; additionally, fat‐free body weight, muscle mass, and basal metabolic rate were significantly lower in the Med group than in the Con group (Figure 2C–E; p < 0.05).
items.extra: What the full-text check said: The body explicitly reports basal metabolic rate as significantly lower in Med after 1 month.

cells:
prednisolone + curcumin placebo  vs  prednisolone placebo + curcumin placebo
Outcome: blood pressure
Direction (first against second): higher

Prednisolone increased HbAlc, insulin, C-peptide, glucagon, blood pressure, mean interstitial glucose, time spent in hyperglycaemia and glucose variability, but no protective effect of curcumin on any of these measures was observed.

Systolic blood pressure was not changed by prednisolone compared to placebo (Group B vs A), and when adding curcumin as a co-treatment, a significant difference in systolic blood pressure was seen compared to the group receiving prednisolone placebo and curcumin placebo (Group C vs A), but not compared to the group receiving prednisolone and curcumin placebo (Group C vs B); thus, curcumin co-treatment had no statistically significant effect.
items.extra: What the full-text check said: The body reports no significant systolic-pressure difference, though diastolic pressure increased.

cells:
interdisciplinary intervention with individualized dietary advice  vs  interdisciplinary intervention including 30 g walnuts/day
Outcome: weight loss at 12 months
Direction (first against second): lower
Weight loss remained greatest in IW at 12 months.
There were no significant differences in weight loss detected between the IW and I groups at either three or 12 months, nor between the I and C groups.
items.extra: What the full-text check said: The body reports no significant weight-loss difference between IW and I at 12 months.

cells:
prolonged time-to-surgery  vs  standard time-to-surgery
Outcome: odynophagia at 6 months postoperatively
Direction (first against second): lower
These benefits were observed at 6 months postoperatively, but not thereafter during follow-up, where no significant differences were observed.
example.extra: What the full-text check said: The 6-month difference was not statistically significant.
example.answer: abstract says more than the body shows
example.why: The record says what the abstract says: the abstract counts less pain on swallowing at 6 months among "these benefits". The body's own table gives 18 against 16 with P = 0.431, so it does not show the difference. The abstract says more than the body shows.

sets.name: 2 Registry
sets.title: A record against the registry
sets.context: For trials that posted results at ClinicalTrials.gov, we compared our record with the posted result for the same two groups and the same outcome. In these items the two disagree.
sets.question: Our record and the result posted at ClinicalTrials.gov for the same two groups and outcome disagree. Is the record at fault?

answers.label: record at fault
answers.meaning: The record is wrong: a direction taken from numbers without a test, a direction for a pair the abstract does not test, or a direction the wrong way.

answers.label: paper and registry report different results
answers.meaning: The record reads the abstract correctly. The registry posts another result for the pair: another time point, another analysis or another measure.

answers.label: cannot tell
answers.meaning: The texts shown, and the paper behind the link, do not settle it.

example.answer: paper and registry report different results

sets.name: 3 Benchmark direction

sets.question: On the Evidence Inference benchmark, our record and the doctors' label give different directions for the same comparison. Which one follows the abstract?
